text:
Rajiv: Quick follow-up to the RFC — I'm drafting an "ownership playbook" that teams can use to decide service boundaries for runtime-related concerns. Wanted to get early feedback before I turn this into a proper RFC PR.
Anya: SGTM. Do you mean one doc that covers tech-debt criteria, cutover patterns, and an ownership matrix? :+1:
Rajiv: Yep. High-level sections I'm thinking: 1) When to extract a service (signal thresholds), 2) Minimal API contract rules, 3) Migration patterns (strangler, dual-write, proxy), 4) Testing & CI expectations, 5) Debt paydown checklist and post-extract observability runbook.
Mike: Make sure to include explicit latency/SLI breakpoints. We've had surprises where a small sync moved to a separate service and killed tail latency because there was no KV cache plan.
Leah: Also add guidance around shared state (KV cache, session vs request-scoped). We should prefer read-only shared caches and make ownership explicit for writes.
Rajiv: Good call. Draft snippet of the migration checklist:
```
- assess: traffic patterns, p95 latency, burst behavior
- contract: define minimal API + backwards compatibility window
- cache: decide ownership (single-writer vs cache-aside)
- rollout: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% (with auto-fallback)
- tests: integration + perf + chaos failure injection
- debt: create paydown ticket (label: infra-debt/ownership)
```
Anya: Love the checklist. For the contract item, can we include a short template? e.g.
```
API contract: POST /v1/score
- inputs: {model_id, prompt, ctx_id}
- outputs: {tokens, latency_ms, model_version}
- invariants: idempotency for repeated ctx_id requests
- deprecation: 4-week preview before breaking changes
```
Mike: We should also require a perf regression sled. Add a bullet under tests: "benchmark before/after on representative payloads" so we don't accidentally regress cost.
Leah: On the 'debt paydown' section, recommend a default window: 3 months for critical debt, 6 months for low-priority. Tie to sprint cadence and include an owner.
Rajiv: Thinking about enforcement: proposal is a lightweight review checkbox on PRs that change ownership-sensitive code + a monthly "ownership shadow" audit from infra. Ops-bot can post a reminder.
ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: monthly ownership-audit -> RINF-ownership-audit (runbook: https://intra.redwood/runs/ownership-audit)
sre-bot: Added SLI smoke tests to the canary job for any service labeled "runtime-owned".
Mike: One tradeoff question — how much do we require teams to split versus allowing a compatibility layer/facade? My vote: prefer facade if latency-critical and the split introduces tail risk; prefer split when deployment independence is the priority.
Anya: Agree on preference heuristics. Maybe add a decision tree in the playbook: deploy independence? yes -> split. Latency-sensitive? yes -> facade-first.
Rajiv: Nice. I'll turn this into a PR next week. Actionables for now:
- Rajiv: draft PR + decision tree (RINF-3214)
- Anya: add contract template examples (small, idempotent endpoints)
- Mike: add perf-sled example and CI checks
- Leah: propose debt window wording and enforcement language
I'll ping y'all when it's up. Thanks! :rocket:
